title: Maximum Length of Pair Chain
statement: Pair [a, b] may follow pair [c, d] when b < c, strictly. Choose pairs in any order and return the length of the longest chain you can form.
constraints: pairs may be used in any order, not the order given
the follow condition is STRICT: [1,2] cannot be followed by [2,3]
hints: This is the same shape as scheduling non-overlapping activities: take as many as possible, and the greedy rule is about which one to finish first.
Sort by the SECOND value. Then walk the list taking any pair that starts strictly after the last one you took ended.
Sorting by the first value instead needs dynamic programming to recover the same answer; sorting by the end makes the greedy choice provably safe, because finishing earliest leaves the most room.

cases.name: a wide pair must be dropped
